comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose high borrower credit quality metrics, specifically focusing on FICO scores and loan performance for wealth/consumer lending, but they apply to different loan products. GS reports that substantially all residential real estate loans in its unrated category had FICO scores >740 and LTV <80% as of Dec 2024. Similarly, BAC discloses that for its consumer card portfolio (which includes excluded small business cards), the majority of the balance ($5.8B) has a refreshed FICO score >=740, indicating a comparable focus on high-credit-quality borrowers, though BAC provides aggregate dollar amounts rather than a performance statement like GS.

sentences.text: • Substantially all residential real estate loans included in the other metrics/unrated category consists of loans extended to wealth management clients. As of both December 2024 and December 2023, substantially all of such loans had a loan-to-value ratio of less than 80% and were performing in accordance with the contractual terms. Additionally, as of both December 2024 and December 2023, the vast majority of such loans had a FICO credit score of greater than 740.

Refreshed FICO scores for this portfolio are $699 million for less than 620; $1.2 billion for greater than or equal to 620 and less than 680; $3.0 billion for greater than or equal to 680 and less than 740; and $5.8 billion greater than or equal to 740.

comparisons.peer_topic: Residential Real Estate Loan Risk Metrics
comparisons.peer_summary: For residential real estate loans, credit quality is assessed using LTV ratios (including combined LTV for junior liens), geographic distribution of collateral, and borrower FICO scores, with higher risk associated with high LTV and low FICO scores.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and JPM utilize LTV ratios and FICO scores as primary metrics to assess the credit quality and risk of residential real estate loans. GS highlights that its unrated residential loans had LTV <80% and FICO >740, implying low risk. JPM explicitly defines LTV as an indicator of potential loss severity and borrower willingness to pay, and FICO as a secondary indicator where scores <660 are considered higher risk. Both disclosures converge on using these specific metrics to characterize the risk profile of residential lending, with GS providing specific outcomes for its high-quality segment and JPM defining the framework for assessing risk across the spectrum.

sentences.text: • Substantially all residential real estate loans included in the other metrics/unrated category consists of loans extended to wealth management clients. As of both December 2024 and December 2023, substantially all of such loans had a loan-to-value ratio of less than 80% and were performing in accordance with the contractual terms. Additionally, as of both December 2024 and December 2023, the vast majority of such loans had a FICO credit score of greater than 740.

• For residential real estate loans, the current estimated LTV ratio, or the combined LTV ratio in the case of junior lien loans, is an indicator of the potential loss severity in the event of default. Additionally, LTV or combined LTV ratios can provide insight into a borrower's continued willingness to pay, as the delinquency rate of high-LTV loans tends to be greater than that for loans where the borrower has equity in the collateral. The geographic distribution of the loan collateral also provides insight as to the credit quality of the portfolio, as factors such as the regional economy, home price changes and specific events such as natural disasters, will affect credit quality. The borrower's current or "refreshed" FICO score is a secondary credit quality indicator for certain loans, as FICO scores are an indication of the borrower's credit payment history. Thus, a loan to a borrower with a low FICO score (less than 660) is considered to be of higher risk than a loan to a borrower with a higher FICO score. Further, a loan to a borrower with a high LTV ratio and a low FICO score is at greater risk of default than a loan to a borrower that has both a high LTV ratio and a high FICO score.

comparisons.peer_topic: Credit quality indicators for various loan types
comparisons.peer_summary: Credit quality indicators include internal risk ratings for corporate and commercial real estate loans, FICO scores and LTV ratios for residential real estate loans, and employment status for employee loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS explicitly list FICO scores and LTV ratios as standard credit quality indicators for their residential real estate loans. GS uses these metrics to characterize the quality of its unrated residential loans (LTV <80%, FICO >740). MS lists these same two metrics (FICO scores and LTV ratios) as the specific indicators considered for residential real estate loans within its Allowance for Credit Losses (ACL) process, confirming a shared industry approach to measuring residential credit risk using these exact variables.
